why: P1 because it closes a real memory-amplification DoS vector where an attacker could make a single peer's orphan cost up to 28x its accounted weight, and reviewers demonstrated a further ~1GB spike bug in the fix itself that has since been patched.
Orphan resolution and 1p1c package relay depend on this working correctly for standard-weight, witness-heavy transactions like BitVM-style scripts.

result.summary: This PR changes how the transaction orphanage stores pending orphan transactions, keeping them serialized rather than deserialized, so that the existing weight-based memory accounting becomes a true upper bound on memory use rather than an underestimate. It adds GetOrphanUsage(), GetParentTxids(), and an id-based GetChildrenFromSamePeer() so callers can work with orphan metadata without forcing deserialization, and updates Find1P1CPackage to materialize only the selected child. It renames DEFAULT_RESERVED_ORPHAN_WEIGHT_PER_PEER to DEFAULT_RESERVED_ORPHAN_USAGE_PER_PEER and adds a regression test for a witness-heavy orphan.
result.problem: Orphan memory accounting assumes weight is often higher than actual memory usage, but that assumption fails badly for transactions with many small witness stack elements: a standard-weight transaction of 199,000 1-byte witness items can use 28x its accounted weight (11.1MB vs 398,247WU), and one such orphan can be retained per peer, letting an attacker inflate a node's real memory use far past the intended per-peer and global caps. This affects every node's DoS resistance to malicious or merely BitVM-style peers.

result.card: This PR changes Bitcoin Core's transaction orphanage to store orphan transactions serialized instead of deserialized, so that the existing weight-based memory accounting becomes a true upper bound on memory rather than an underestimate. It fixes a real DoS amplification: a standard-weight transaction with 199,000 1-byte witness elements previously used 28x its accounted weight in memory (11.1MB vs ~400,000WU), retainable once per peer, confirmed independently by reviewer jeanpablojp's benchmarks. During review, instagibbs proposed the serialized-storage approach adopted here in place of the author's original weight-metric swap, and later found a second amplification bug in the new Find1P1CPackage code (up to ~1GB spike) which the author fixed in the latest push. Agreement is strong: three concept ACKs, a tested ACK on an earlier revision, and every substantive objection raised has been addressed with code changes. The PR touches the same orphanage files as the open PR #35919 and complements #35923, though no hard dependency is stated; it appears Ready with no known unresolved question.
